issues.text: The definition rests on 'model', but no list I know defines it in this sense. The only entry I have is 'domain model': rules as methods in the class that holds the data. Keycloak's realm file has no methods or rules, so I can't tell if 'sign-in model' means that or just 'what one side keeps about a person, and its words'. I have to guess from the two examples.
issues.quote: a boundary inside which one model and its language apply; outside it, the same word may mean something else, and that is not an error.
issues.fix: In the bounded context bullet, add one plain sentence saying what 'model' means here, e.g. 'A model here is what one part of the system keeps about the business: its things, their fields and the words for them; it need not be a domain model with methods.'

issues.text: Core concepts calls a bounded context a boundary that a model applies inside. Here a model 'is' a bounded context. I stopped to ask if the context is the boundary or the model itself.
issues.quote: Each model is a bounded context, and each count answers its own question correctly.
issues.fix: Replace with 'Each model applies inside its own bounded context, and each count answers its own question correctly.'

issues.text: The block shows `enabled` and `"temporary": false`, and the prose never says what they are. The Try it suggested answer then lists `enabled` as a sign-in-only field, so I'm expected to classify a field I was never told about.
issues.quote: Look at what this model cares about: how she signs in (`username`, `credentials`), whether her email was checked, and which realm role she has.
issues.fix: Add 'whether the account is switched on (`enabled`)' to that list of what the model cares about, or drop `enabled` from the suggested answer.

issues.text: q6: the context lists three proposals and options a, c and d are those three. b is the only option that changes nothing, and the lesson's message is that nothing is wrong. I can pick b from the shape of the options without weighing them.
issues.quote: Keep both models linked by `identity_subject`, and count the report from `customers`.
issues.fix: Replace one distractor with an option that also keeps both models but counts from the wrong side, e.g. 'Keep both models, and count the report from the users in `keycloak/donhang-realm.json`.' (that count includes staff Lan).
